RESULTS May 11, 2026 CP Axtra CPAXT TB / CPAXT.BK Beat, but cost pressure ahead Sector: Commerce NEUTRAL Rating: HOLD Target Price: Bt17.00 Price (May 8, 2026): Bt14.70 Core profit beat our estimate and the street CPAXT reported a 1Q26 core profit of Bt2.79bn, up by 6% YoY and 9% QoQ, beating our estimate and the Bloomberg consensus. The beat was mainly due to gains of Bt240-250m tied to the reversal of a merchandise inventory impairment and FX hedging. The YoY growth was driven by two factors. First, the Aug 2025 consolidation of Renewed Hope Group (a Malaysian food service firm ) boosted wholesale b iz sales. Wholesale, which c omprised 52% of CPAXT’s 1Q26 EBIT, posted an operating profit of Bt2.52bn, up 6% YoY. Second, financ ial costs declined by 8% YoY, in line with lower interest rates. The QoQ improvement mainly reflected the easing of large merchandise inventory impairments at the retail b iz. Retail co mprised 48% of CPAXT’s 1Q26 EBIT. Note that CPAXT booked about Bt850m of merchandise inventory impairments to its 4Q25 financial statements. Result highlights Consolidated sales totaled Bt130.7bn in 1Q26 , up by 5% YoY and 2% QoQ. Growth was led by makro (57% of sales). Wholesale sales rose by 6% YoY, supported by the consolidation of Renewed Hope Group, two new stores, and 0.6% SSSG. Retail sales grew by 3% YoY, driven by store expansion, with s ales space up 4% YoY to 1.89m sq.m , retail SSS was flat, a clear improvement from a 7.6% decline in 4Q25, helped by FMCG panic-buying in Mar on concerns over price hike risk. Blended GM was 14.1%, down 40bps YoY but up 20bps QoQ, due to the easing of inventory provisions. Wholesale GM declined by 30bps YoY on clearance sales and a bigger proportion of slim-margin dry food in the sales mix. Retail GM slipped by 50bps YoY, squeezed by bigger inventory provisions in Thailand and a bigger proportion of slim-margin products in the sales mix, mainly dry food and alcoholic drinks. Outlook Looking to 2Q26, core earnings should decline both YoY and QoQ, squeezed by Happitat start-up expenses and a full-quarter hit from higher energy costs. Hilltop Offices, part of the Happitat real estate project , opened in Apr. We expect Happitat to book a Bt600m loss for 2026. What has changed? 1Q26 core profit comprises 27% of our 2026 core earnings forecast of Bt10.3bn (up 10% YoY ), close to the 1Q25 proportion of 2025 profit of 28%. Recommendation We maintain our HOLD call, as operation

From: Kiatnakin Phatra Sales Team

Subject: KKPS Sales Note 26 Aug: KTC - U/G PO to Bt43 | CPALL/CPAXT – Diverging 3Q 
outlook | BofA earnings revision - Thailand leads Asia earnings upgrades | 
NVDA – Balance sheet disclosure is the key catalyst 
 

--- page 2 ---
 
 
CPALL/CPAXT – Diverging 3Q outlook 
Yesterday, we hosted one-on-one meetings with CPALL and CPAXT for a local fund. Feedback 
from CPALL was relatively positive. QTD SSSG is around 2%. SSSG was slightly negative in 
June following the launch of the “Thai Chuay Thai” co-payment scheme, but turned positive in 
July and August. Management also expects stronger margin expansion in 3Q26 than in 2Q26, 
supported by easing energy costs. 
 
CPAXT’s outlook remains weaker. Management guided for mid-single-digit negative SSSG 
in 3Q26, with margins also likely to contract due to negative operating leverage. As a result, 
3Q26 earnings are expected to decline YoY, creating downside risk to both our and 
consensus forecasts. Simply put, CPALL’s earnings remain supported by 7-Eleven, with limited 
downside risk, while CPAXT’s earnings forecasts are more vulnerable. We continue to prefer 
CRC as our top pick in the commerce sector.
